title: As AI reshapes newsrooms, leading media outlets are charting different paths for its use
tldr: Major publishers are diverging sharply on how they deploy generative AI in editorial work, with the Guardian episode as a flashpoint. It maps the emerging fault lines between efficiency and trust in journalism.
why_fresh: emerging divergence in newsroom AI policy
angle: Write about what publisher AI policies reveal about content governance choices every comms team will soon face.

title: How one newsletter writer is building a subscription business when "paywalls don't really work"
tldr: A solo journalist grew a public-records newsletter using a quirky seal mascot and community over hard paywalls. A concrete case study in human-centered audience building.
angle: Break down why personality and mascots beat paywalls for niche audience loyalty.

title: Inside Away's new 'programming' strategy for social media
tldr: Luggage brand Away is treating its social channels like a media network with recurring 'programming' rather than one-off posts. A tangible content-strategy shift for brands.
angle: Argue brands should build editorial programming, not post calendars — with Away as the template.

title: Consumers don't experience channels
tldr: A reframing of omnichannel thinking: people don't perceive media in the silos marketers plan around. Directly relevant to how audiences actually consume content.
angle: Explore designing content around lived audience experience, not internal channel org charts.

title: I Tracked 13,184 AI Citations Across 4 LLMs: Here's What I Learned
tldr: Original research on what content actually gets cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and others. Data-driven answer to the AEO/AI-visibility question everyone's guessing about.
angle: Turn the citation data into a practical playbook for making content LLM-visible.

title: 74% of Shoppers Use AI for Discovery—NIQ Report on the Consumer Purchase Journey
tldr: New NIQ research finds a majority of shoppers now use AI tools for product discovery, reshaping the funnel. A hard data point on shifting media-consumption behavior.
angle: What 74% AI discovery means for content architecture and top-of-funnel storytelling.

title: AI Traffic Conversion Rates: New Research from 97 B2B Websites and 29M visits
tldr: Benchmark study showing how visitors from AI search convert differently than traditional search traffic. Useful, evidence-based ROI framing for the AI-search era.
angle: Reframe AI-search skeptics with real conversion data on AI-referred visitors.

title: Why ABC Self-Censored
tldr: In litigation, ABC admits it made coverage decisions under government pressure — a rare, striking admission with big implications for editorial independence and reputation.
angle: On the reputational cost when media brands trade independence for political safety.

title: Lesson No. 1 from Good Good Golf: Context matters in brand storytelling
tldr: A breakdown of the Good Good Golf ad fiasco showing how missing context can capsize a brand narrative. A concrete crisis-and-storytelling case study.
angle: Use Good Good to show how context gaps turn creative into crisis.

title: 'Just Be a Real Person First. Reporters Forget to Do That.'
tldr: The Michigan Chronicle's Sam Robinson on human-first interviewing during a charged election cycle. A reminder that humanity beats polish in earning trust.
angle: Apply 'be a real person first' to brand and comms interviewing and story scouting.

title: 1,000 more job cuts at WPP show the holdco model being reshaped by AI
tldr: WPP's fresh round of layoffs signals AI structurally reshaping the agency holding-company model. A bellwether for where creative and comms work is heading.
angle: What AI-driven agency cuts mean for in-house content and comms teams.

title: Botsitting and botshitting: The new workplace behaviours costing employees 6.4 hours a week
tldr: New research names emerging AI-at-work behaviors — babysitting bad AI output ('botsitting') and generating filler ('botshitting') — draining hours weekly. Sharp lens on real AI adoption friction.
angle: On the hidden content-ops tax of low-quality AI output that teams must clean up.

title: How AI could kill 'corporate ick'
tldr: Voice-first AI tools could let workers talk through emails, memos and posts instead of over-polishing them, potentially making corporate communication more human. Ties tech to a humanity-of-content angle.
angle: Can AI actually make corporate writing sound more human, not less?

title: SU's Creator Economy class talks social media business amid center expansion
tldr: Syracuse is formalizing creator-economy education as universities build dedicated centers. A signal that creator work is institutionalizing into a real discipline.
angle: What formal creator-economy education signals about the maturing of content careers.
